offer: $500 Lineage Founding Pilot for the first 5 external design partners

linkedin.text: AI coding agents are getting fast enough that version control is becoming a coordination problem, not just a storage problem. We built Evercraft Lineage to keep competing agent work from silently overwriting history, preserve who or what changed something and why, verify integrity, and keep GitHub connected as a mirror. The first commercial wedge is intentionally small: one authorized repo, a private Control Room, stale-writer protection, provenance/rationale, semantic diffs, Git import/export, and a closeout architecture packet. First 5 external design partners: $500 one-time. We are not calling this self-serve SaaS yet. It is a human-confirmed founding pilot.

x.text: Two coding agents start from the same commit. Agent A advances the branch. Agent B tries to write from the stale head. Lineage refuses the silent overwrite and preserves B's proposed commit for reconciliation. That's the $500 founding pilot: governed multi-agent history while GitHub stays connected.

discussion.opener: Curious how teams running 2+ coding agents are handling history races today. Worktrees isolate files, but what are you using for agent identity, rationale, stale-writer detection, and a durable record of rejected/competing work?
discussion.boundary: Use for genuine discussion. Do not astroturf, fabricate usage, or hide Evercraft affiliation when mentioning Lineage.
